svg.title: Groundhog Day
svg.desc: Worlds and Thread atlas. Story order progresses downward. Connections use reserved routing space. Full relationship and citation ledgers follow the chart. The HTML companion contains the complete accessible model.
svg.text: P3 closed loop - mind persists across resets
2.5D · cabinet axonometric · depth separates surfaces only · Story-order ranks, not elapsed time. Equal ranks do not assert physical
Amber S± — Split outcomes. + and − are signs, not fates.
Blue T — Directed transfers. B body · M memory · C consciousness · S signal · ? literal/unspecified mechanism.
Emerald V / L — Numbered visits and explicit links only. Emerald centre on a cable means the route follows that connection.
Slate rail — World identity. Cutoff means chart boundary, not destruction. Crossings are bridges; only markers are joins.
Evidence / fate — [n] opens the evidence record. × dead · ● alive · ? unknown · ∅ nonexistent. Purple dotted connections are

{"id": "canon", "kind": "canon_statement", "text": "Phil relives February 2 in Punxsutawney. His body resets; his memory
persists. The film represents three iterations (opening day, an exhausted stretch, the changed man) of an uncounted larger
number. No other world exists; the loop ends when his day stops repeating.", "title": "Groundhog Day (1993), theatrical cut"}
{"id": "allocation", "kind": "test_fixture", "text": "Iteration count beyond the three represented days is unknown and labeled
as such. Rita fates are tracked per represented iteration.", "title": "Fixture allocations"}

svg.text: Iterations are revisions of one world, not universes.
